title: Our Memory is not The Reality
excerpt: Did you notice, at some point in your life, that a memory of some event ended up changing, even in your own recollection? I realized that years ago and it was surprising. I am kind of a story-teller, and one of the main abilities for being one is to create a narrative about the story, diminish parts of the story and amplify others in order to make the story appealing and interesting. However, as you keep telling the same story, you keep improving it, stressing more and more the important parts and skipping the irrelevant parts. But notice this: the irrelevant parts are not irrelevant in what happened, they are "irrelevant" in regards of the story telling. And that's what I noticed: stories evolve and change as you keep learning what works and what not, they are still the same basic facts, but the way they are told make them more important than they were in reality.

title: When I fell in Love with Computers
excerpt: I was 11 and I didn't have a PC. Many friends had a 386 or even a 486. I was reading PC magazines -PC World is the one I remember the most- for a year or more already. It started out of pure interest, from a child that looked at those machines like something magic. Maybe the reason was the good memories I had with the Spectrum ZX of my uncle when my cousin and I were 8 years old. But I didn't have a computer, it was what it was. Expensive thing those computers.
